key_insight: The paper shows that the Hessian spectrum of linear neural networks depends explicitly on dataset structure, with sharpness tied to the largest class proportion in classification with MSE loss.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a data-dependent way to anticipate optimization difficulty and curvature, informing initialization, training stability, and second-order method design.
method: Derive closed-form Hessian eigenvalues for linear networks with arbitrary depth, width, samples, features, and labels.
Analyze classification with MSE loss to link maximum class imbalance to solution sharpness.
Test robustness by relaxing idealized assumptions and adding nonlinearities in experiments.
evidence_signal: The authors empirically validate the theory and report that the predictions remain robust across many practical settings.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees are derived for linear networks and MSE-based classification, so behavior may differ when losses, architectures, or data regimes deviate substantially.
paper_title: How the Hessian-Spectrum of Neural Networks Depends on Data
